A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Part2GS, with matching authors, research objectives, and core experiments. All pages, including appendices, were readable through text extraction and visual inspection, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction and articulation results, component ablations, qualitative examples, and runtime measurements in Tables 1–4 and associated figures.

after.justification: V2 retains the original empirical results and adds cumulative ablations, sensitivity studies, photometric comparisons, and additional qualitative results.

M1.justification: The core canonicalization, part embeddings, SE(3) articulation, repel points, and physical losses remain. V2 omits v1's Mahalanobis initialization and separate consistency loss, presents a joint objective, and documents soft transformation assignment and force clamping. The PDFs do not establish which differences represent changed procedures versus revisions to the earlier incomplete description.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same PARIS, DTA-Multi, and ArtGS-Multi articulated-object coverage, including real fridge and storage examples. Additional illustrations remain within household-object articulation; photometric scoring, motion-type breakdowns, and internal parameter perturbations do not establish new task or input-environment coverage.

E2.justification: Matched benchmark comparisons retain Ditto, PARIS, DTA, and ArtGS in Table 1 and DTA and ArtGS in Table 2. Runtime and part-discovery comparisons also retain their comparators. New evaluations reuse existing comparison methods and introduce internal ablation controls.

E3.justification: V2 substantially expands evaluation protocols with cumulative component additions, part-count and repel-point sweeps, noisy initialization, periodic repel-point refresh, and force-exponent tests. It also introduces PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, and penetration measurements. These are additional protocols; the retained benchmark results do not establish changed original evaluation settings.

E4.justification: V1's removal ablation survives as v2 Table 8. V2 adds cumulative ablations, individual physical-loss analyses, global versus per-part canonical weighting, part-count sensitivity, repel-point count/noise/update studies, force-exponent sensitivity, and motion-type analysis. These substantially broaden investigation of component contributions and robustness.

E5.justification: V1 reports means and gives both 10-trial and 3-trial descriptions without uncertainty entries. V2 adds plus/minus values for DTA, ArtGS, and Part2GS in Table 1 and t-tests with n=3 across 111 object-metric pairs. This establishes expanded statistical reporting, not an increase in experimental runs.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain their numerical means, and the original removal-ablation and runtime values are preserved. V2 adds substantial results from new ablations, robustness studies, and photometric evaluation. For example, Table 15 newly reports Foldchair PSNR of 33.6 for Part2GS versus 32.4 for ArtGS; this is not a performance improvement over v1.

T1.justification: V2 explicitly defines the motion-richness interpolation coefficient and adds probability-weighted transformation and clipped-force formulas in Appendix A. V1's Mahalanobis and separate consistency-loss definitions disappear. These are limited changes to mathematical specification; neither version contains a theorem-and-proof contribution.

C1.justification: The principal part-aware reconstruction contributions and up-to-10× movable-part Chamfer claim remain. V2 more explicitly claims joint optimization of geometry, part discovery, and articulation, and its introduction calls the interpolation coefficient learnable, whereas v1 calls it fixed. That wording conflicts with v2 Appendix A's once-per-object computation, so it does not establish a corresponding implementation change.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive explanations of part-count misspecification, global canonical weighting, repulsion stability, and individual physical losses, including disclosure of a user-specified part-count bound. It removes v1 Appendix E's limitations concerning paired observations and indistinguishable part motions. It also adds stronger interpretations, including a 4–10× gain over ArtGS in Section 5.1 that the retained tables do not support.

D1.justification: V2 Appendix A substantially expands implementation disclosure: soft training assignments and hard inference assignments, force safeguards, loss weights, Adam learning rate, 2,000 repel points, proximity threshold, and 30k/5k initialization iterations. However, v1's RTX 4090 hardware statement, 10K-point Chamfer sampling specification, and detailed dataset provenance are omitted. The project link remains.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations including GaussianFlow, ST-4DGS, GaussianArt, and ReArtGS, and sharpens the contrast with continuous non-rigid Gaussian modeling. MultiScan and SAPIEN references disappear with the dataset-detail discussion. The central positioning around part-aware, physically guided articulated reconstruction remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The method changes from two principal subsections to four, the main ablation narrative becomes cumulative, and the appendices are substantially reorganized. These constitute broad narrative and structural revision beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column layout, adds a teaser, redraws the pipeline overview, expands qualitative displays, and adds numerous experimental tables. Existing material is also relocated: the removal ablation becomes Table 8, runtime becomes Table 7, and the earlier appendix part-discovery montage moves into the main text.

improvement.justification: V2 supplies valuable implementation details and targeted robustness and photometric evidence missing from v1. However, it removes substantive failure conditions and introduces unresolved inconsistencies: clean Table (5 parts) angular error is 0.30 in Tables 11–12 but 0.03 in Tables 2 and 13, while Section 5.1's new 4–10× gain over ArtGS is unsupported by the unchanged benchmark values. These problems affect confidence in the added evidence, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
